title: Multiplayer Infra Setup
author: HauntingSquirrel8818
selftext:
AI Game devs - what is the online multiplayer setup that you are using for your game? How difficult was the set up? 

I am curious as to what multiplayer set up can support the increasingly high quality vibe coded games (especially with the launch of Astra and Opus 5.5), without significant latency issues.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
The major problem here is that multiplayer will be different for different games. You have your turn-based games like chess or Hearthstone, your high-latency games like StarCraft, and your highly sensitive action games like Quake or Street Fighter.

Then there are games which are match-based, 1v1, or persistent worlds, or have all sorts of different systems.

And a game looking “high quality” is not enough, because it takes time and effort to build a player base. Most vibe coded games do not have many players.

replies.author: HauntingSquirrel8818
replies.body: Yes, totally understand that. I have built both turn based games and real time games, and are using a host-authoritative architecture with a websocket + webRTC reliable/unreliable dual path, with decent performance on latency even for the real time games. So I am wondering what creators here are using for their multiplayer games especially those with high quality graphics created by the latest models (understand your point about user base, but i was referring to graphics in my post) and whether multiplayer latency and performance still worked well in these games.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: What does graphics have to do with it?
